# MoroAI — Comprehensive Documentation for LLMs

> MoroAI is a local-first model adaptation foundry for small language models.
> Apache-2.0 licensed, open-source Python CLI + web dashboard.
> Website: https://moroai.cc · GitHub: https://github.com/moroai/moro


# SECTION: Getting Started


## Document: /docs/getting-started/first-model/

<div class="not-prose mb-8">
    <span class="text-xs font-mono font-bold text-moro-400 uppercase tracking-wider bg-moro-500/10 px-2.5 py-1 rounded border border-moro-500/20 mb-3 inline-block">
      Hands-On Tutorial
    </span>
    <h1 class="text-3xl sm:text-5xl font-black text-white tracking-tight">Your First Local Model</h1>
    <p class="text-gray-400 text-base mt-2">
      From custom private JSONL logs to a fully functioning local LLM assistant in under 10 minutes.
    </p>
  </div>

  <h2>1. Prepare Your Domain Dataset</h2>
  <p>
    MoroAI accepts standard chat message formats (compatible with OpenAI and Hugging Face ShareGPT/ChatML formats). Create a file called <code>./data/raw/finance_qa.jsonl</code>:
  </p>

  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300">
{`{"messages": [{"role": "system", "content": "You are a corporate financial analyst assistant."}, {"role": "user", "content": "What is our company policy on capital expenditure approval limits?"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "Under Section 4.2 of our Financial Guidelines, CapEx under $50,000 requires Department Head sign-off; amounts between $50,000 and $250,000 require CFO approval; exceeding $250,000 requires Board of Directors authorization."}]}
{"messages": [{"role": "system", "content": "You are a corporate financial analyst assistant."}, {"role": "user", "content": "How are international wire transfer exchange fees recognized?"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "Foreign exchange wire transaction fees are recognized under Account 6420 (Bank & Transaction Fees) at the spot rate on the date of settlement."}]}`}
  </pre>

  <h2>2. Compile the Dataset with Epistemic Filtering</h2>
  <p>
    Run the compiler to calculate token information entropy, filter duplicates, and protect rare financial guidelines:
  </p>

  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300">
moro data build --source ./data/raw/finance_qa.jsonl --output ./data/compiled/
  </pre>

  <p>
    The compiler outputs <code>curated_train.jsonl</code> and <code>curated_val.jsonl</code> with quality metrics.
  </p>

  <h2>3. Hardware Audit & Training</h2>
  <p>
    Generate the configuration and initiate training:
  </p>

  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300">
moro recipe generate --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B --hardware detect
moro train
  </pre>

  <p>
    MoroAI will automatically allocate GPU tensors, optimize batch sizes, and monitor convergence with loss telemetry.
  </p>

  <h2>4. Test Local Inference</h2>
  <p>
    Once training finishes, export the model and test prompt completion immediately:
  </p>

  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-emerald-400">
moro release deploy --target ollama --model-name finance-assistant:v1
ollama run finance-assistant:v1 "Who needs to approve a $120,000 server purchase?"
  </pre>

  <div class="not-prose mt-12 pt-6 border-t border-dark-800 flex items-center justify-between">
    <a href="/docs/getting-started/quickstart/" class="text-xs font-semibold text-gray-400 hover:text-white transition-colors">
      ← Quickstart
    </a>
    <a href="/docs/concepts/overview/" class="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-5 py-2.5 rounded-xl bg-moro-500 hover:bg-moro-400 text-white font-semibold text-xs transition-colors">
      <span>Next: System Overview</span>
      <ArrowRight class="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
    </a>
  </div>

## Document: /docs/getting-started/installation/

<div class="not-prose mb-8">
    <span class="text-xs font-mono font-bold text-moro-400 uppercase tracking-wider bg-moro-500/10 px-2.5 py-1 rounded border border-moro-500/20 mb-3 inline-block">
      Setup & Verification
    </span>
    <h1 class="text-3xl sm:text-5xl font-black text-white tracking-tight">Installation Guide</h1>
    <p class="text-gray-400 text-base mt-2">
      Step-by-step installation instructions for Linux, macOS (Apple Silicon), and Windows WSL2.
    </p>
  </div>

  <h2>System Prerequisites</h2>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Python:</strong> Version 3.10, 3.11, or 3.12</li>
    <li><strong>RAM:</strong> 8GB minimum (16GB+ recommended for dataset compilation)</li>
    <li><strong>Disk Space:</strong> 10GB free SSD space for base model weights and cached adapters</li>
    <li><strong>GPU (Optional for training):</strong> NVIDIA GPU with 4GB+ VRAM or Apple Silicon Mac (M1/M2/M3/M4)</li>
  </ul>

  <h2>Installation Methods</h2>

  <h3>Option 1: Standard `pip` (Recommended)</h3>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300">
# Basic installation (CLI, data compiler, and evaluation)
pip install moroai

# With training extensions (PyTorch, BitsAndBytes, PEFT, TRL)
pip install "moroai[train]"

# Full installation with all optional export and serving plugins
pip install "moroai[all]"
  </pre>

  <h3>Option 2: From Source (Latest Development)</h3>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300">
git clone https://github.com/moroai/moro.git
cd moro
pip install -e ".[train]"
  </pre>

  <h3>Option 3: Pre-Built Docker Image</h3>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300">
docker pull moroai/moro:latest
docker run --gpus all -it -p 3000:3000 moroai/moro:latest
  </pre>

  <h2>Verifying Installation (`moro doctor`)</h2>
  <p>Run the built-in diagnostic tool to verify all components:</p>

  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-emerald-300 leading-relaxed">
$ moro doctor

MoroAI System Diagnostics
─────────────────────────────────────────────────
Platform:         Darwin / Linux (x86_64 or arm64)
Python:           3.11.5 (Active environment)
CLI Version:      0.1.0 (moro)

Core Dependencies:
  ✓ typer         0.12.0
  ✓ rich          13.7.0
  ✓ pydantic      2.6.0
  ✓ pyyaml        6.0.1

Training Backend:
  ✓ torch         2.2.0 (CUDA 12.1 or MPS available)
  ✓ transformers  4.38.0
  ✓ peft          0.9.0
  ✓ bitsandbytes  0.42.0

Hardware Status:
  ✓ GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (12,288 MB VRAM)
  ✓ Driver: 545.29.06 | CUDA: 12.1
  ✓ Zero-OOM Pre-Flight Engine: ACTIVE

System Verdict:
  ✓ READY FOR DATA CURATION & LOCAL TRAINING
  </pre>

    </table>
  </div>

  <h2>Common Installation Troubleshooting</h2>

  <h3>1. CUDA Not Found or PyTorch CPU-Only Installed</h3>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-orange-300">
# Verify NVIDIA driver is working:
nvidia-smi

# Reinstall PyTorch with explicit CUDA 12.1 runtime:
pip install --upgrade torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121
  </pre>

  <h3>2. Apple Silicon Metal Performance Shaders (MPS) Setup</h3>
  <p>On macOS with Apple Silicon chips, hardware acceleration is enabled out of the box through PyTorch's Metal backend:</p>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300">
python -c "import torch; print('MPS available:', torch.backends.mps.is_available())"
  </pre>

## Document: /docs/getting-started/introduction/

<div class="not-prose mb-8">
    <div class="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-3 py-1 rounded-full bg-moro-500/10 border border-moro-500/20 text-moro-400 text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider mb-4">
      <Sparkles class="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
      <span>Getting Started</span>
    </div>
    <h1 class="text-3xl sm:text-5xl font-black text-white tracking-tight">Introduction to MoroAI</h1>
    <p class="text-gray-400 text-base mt-2">
      The local-first platform for turning uncurated enterprise data into high-yield, sovereign language models.
    </p>
  </div>

  <h2>What is MoroAI?</h2>
  <p>
    <strong>MoroAI</strong> is an open-source, local-first model adaptation foundry. It transforms proprietary documents, customer interaction logs, code repositories, and structured databases into dependable, fine-tuned language models on consumer hardware.
  </p>

  <p>
    Existing tools like Axolotl, Unsloth, or LLaMA-Factory provide scripts for running backpropagation, but leave data curation, hardware sizing, evaluation, and release governance to manual guesswork. MoroAI automates the entire lifecycle end-to-end:
  </p>

  <div class="grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 gap-4 not-prose my-6">
    <div class="p-5 rounded-2xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800">
      <div class="font-bold text-white mb-1">1. Epistemic Data Curation</div>
      <p class="text-xs text-gray-400">Protects rare domain corner cases with Mutual Information Guard while filtering redundant noise.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="p-5 rounded-2xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800">
      <div class="font-bold text-white mb-1">2. Zero-OOM Hardware Prediction</div>
      <p class="text-xs text-gray-400">Simulates activation and gradient memory before launch, guaranteeing zero Out-Of-Memory crashes.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="p-5 rounded-2xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800">
      <div class="font-bold text-white mb-1">3. Self-Healing Training</div>
      <p class="text-xs text-gray-400">5-step autonomous recovery engine that catches spikes, clears caches, and resumes without data loss.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="p-5 rounded-2xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800">
      <div class="font-bold text-white mb-1">4. Instant Ollama & GGUF Release</div>
      <p class="text-xs text-gray-400">One-command quantize and deploy with full cryptographic Software Bill of Materials (SBOM).</p>
    </div>
  </div>

  <h2>Who is MoroAI for?</h2>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Regulated Enterprises:</strong> Legal, financial, defense, and healthcare teams unable to send proprietary data to cloud APIs.</li>
    <li><strong>Engineers with Consumer GPUs:</strong> Builders fine-tuning 1.5B–14B models on single RTX 3060, 4070, or Apple Silicon M-series chips.</li>
    <li><strong>MLOps Teams:</strong> Teams needing cryptographic audit logs, deterministic regression tests, and continuous DPO feedback loops.</li>
  </ul>

  <div class="not-prose mt-12 pt-6 border-t border-dark-800 flex items-center justify-between">
    <span class="text-xs text-gray-500">Next Step</span>
    <a
      href="/docs/getting-started/installation/"
      class="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-5 py-2.5 rounded-xl bg-moro-500 hover:bg-moro-400 text-white font-semibold text-xs transition-colors"
    >
      <span>Installation Guide</span>
      <ArrowRight class="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
    </a>
  </div>

## Document: /docs/getting-started/quickstart/

<div class="not-prose mb-8">
    <span class="text-xs font-mono font-bold text-moro-400 uppercase tracking-wider bg-moro-500/10 px-2.5 py-1 rounded border border-moro-500/20 mb-3 inline-block">
      5-Minute Tutorial
    </span>
    <h1 class="text-3xl sm:text-5xl font-black text-white tracking-tight">Quickstart: 5 Minutes to Your First Local Model</h1>
    <p class="text-gray-400 text-base mt-2">
      This step-by-step tutorial takes you from <strong class="text-white">zero to a deployed, private local language model</strong> in 5 minutes.
    </p>
  </div>

  <h2>Step 1: Install MoroAI (30 seconds)</h2>
  <p>Install the MoroAI core package with training extensions:</p>

  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300">
# Install with training support
pip install "moroai[train]"
  </pre>

  <p>Verify that your environment and GPU are ready:</p>

  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-emerald-300">
moro doctor
  </pre>

  <h2>Step 2: Initialize Your Project (30 seconds)</h2>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300">
moro init my-first-model
cd my-first-model
  </pre>

  <p>This creates a reproducible workspace:</p>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-gray-300">
my-first-model/
├── moro.yaml          # Project configuration & recipe
├── data/
│   └── raw/           # Raw training data inputs
├── runs/              # Training checkpoints & telemetry
├── releases/          # Exported GGUF models & SBOMs
└── eval/              # Evaluation suites
  </pre>

  <h2>Step 3: Add Your Data (1 minute)</h2>
  <p>Create a sample customer support dataset:</p>

  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-cyan-300">
cat &gt; data/raw/support_data.jsonl &lt;&lt; 'EOF'
{`{"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "How do I reset my password?"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "Go to Settings > Security > Reset Password."}]}`}
{`{"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is your refund policy?"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "We offer a 30-day money-back guarantee on all purchases."}]}`}
{`{"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "How do I contact support?"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "You can reach our support team at support@example.com."}]}`}
EOF
  </pre>

  <p>Ensure <code>moro.yaml</code> references your raw data:</p>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300">
dataset:
  source: ./data/raw/support_data.jsonl
  format: jsonl
  </pre>

  <h2>Step 4: Build the Dataset with MI Guard (30 seconds)</h2>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300">
moro data build
  </pre>

  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-emerald-300">
✓ Loaded 3 samples
✓ After deduplication: 3 samples
✓ MI Guard: 1 rare domain landmark protected
✓ Split: train=2, val=1, eval=0
✓ Dataset compiled to data/compiled
  </pre>

  <h2>Step 5: Train Your Model (2 minutes)</h2>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300">
moro train
  </pre>

  <p>MoroAI detects your hardware, audits VRAM memory safety, and runs local fine-tuning:</p>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-purple-300">
✓ Hardware detected: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (12GB)
✓ Recipe generated: lora_r=16, lr=2e-4, batch=2, accum=8
✓ Training started: run_1234567890
✓ Step 50/100 | Loss: 1.42 | VRAM: 6.2GB
✓ Training completed in 45s (Zero OOM)
  </pre>

  <h2>Step 6: Deploy to Ollama (30 seconds)</h2>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-teal-300">
moro release export --run-id run_1234567890 --version v1.0.0
moro release deploy --target ollama --version v1.0.0
  </pre>

  <h2>Step 7: Test Your Private Model (30 seconds)</h2>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300">
{`# Test locally via Ollama CLI:
ollama run my-first-model:v1.0.0 "How do I reset my password?"

# Or via the OpenAI-compatible local REST API:
curl http://localhost:11434/api/generate -d '{
  "model": "my-first-model:v1.0.0",
  "prompt": "How do I reset my password?",
  "stream": false
}'`}
  </pre>

  <h2>What Just Happened?</h2>
  <div class="not-prose my-6 grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
    <div class="p-4 rounded-xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800">
      <div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-1.5 text-cyan-400 font-bold text-xs">
        <Database class="w-4 h-4" />
        <span>Data Curated</span>
      </div>
      <p class="text-gray-400 text-xs">
        Raw data was parsed, deduplicated, and scored with information-theoretic token density.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="p-4 rounded-xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800">
      <div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-1.5 text-emerald-400 font-bold text-xs">
        <Cpu class="w-4 h-4" />
        <span>Hardware Aware</span>
      </div>
      <p class="text-gray-400 text-xs">
        An optimal LoRA recipe was synthesized to guarantee zero out-of-memory crashes on your GPU.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="p-4 rounded-xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800">
      <div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-1.5 text-purple-400 font-bold text-xs">
        <Rocket class="w-4 h-4" />
        <span>Model Deployed</span>
      </div>
      <p class="text-gray-400 text-xs">
        Adapter weights were quantized to GGUF format and registered directly into the local Ollama runtime.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="p-4 rounded-xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800">
      <div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-1.5 text-emerald-400 font-bold text-xs">
        <Check class="w-4 h-4" />
        <span>100% Private</span>
      </div>
      <p class="text-gray-400 text-xs">
        Zero tokens, weights, or logs left your workstation. Complete data sovereignty achieved.
      </p>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="not-prose mt-12 pt-6 border-t border-dark-800 flex items-center justify-between">
    <a href="/docs/getting-started/installation/" class="text-xs font-semibold text-gray-400 hover:text-white transition-colors">

      <span>Deep First Model Guide</span>
      <ArrowRight class="w-3.5 h-3.5" />

# SECTION: Concepts & Architecture


## Document: /docs/concepts/dashboard/

<div class="not-prose mb-8">
    <span class="text-xs font-mono font-bold text-pink-400 uppercase tracking-wider bg-pink-500/10 px-2.5 py-1 rounded border border-pink-500/20 mb-3 inline-block">
      Subsystem 07
    </span>
    <h1 class="text-3xl sm:text-5xl font-black text-white tracking-tight">Mission Control UI</h1>
    <p class="text-gray-400 text-base mt-2">
      Zero-cloud, browser-based command center for visual dataset curation, live VRAM and loss telemetry, model evaluation diffing, and one-click Ollama deployment.
    </p>
  </div>

  <h2>System Architecture & Local Execution</h2>
  <p>
    While the <code>moro</code> CLI provides complete automation for scripting and CI/CD pipelines, complex fine-tuning operations benefit immensely from visual, real-time feedback. MoroAI provides <strong>Mission Control</strong>: a self-contained web application served entirely from the local Python package.
  </p>
  
  <p>
    When launched with <code>moro dashboard</code>, the system starts an embedded, high-performance ASGI server (Uvicorn + FastAPI) and binds exclusively to <code>localhost</code> (or a user-specified private subnet interface). No telemetry or tracking scripts are loaded; assets are served locally from the package distribution.
  </p>

  <div class="not-prose my-6 p-5 rounded-2xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs">
    <div class="text-gray-400 border-b border-dark-800 pb-2 mb-3 flex items-center justify-between">
      <span>Launch Command</span>
      <span class="text-pink-400">moro dashboard</span>
    </div>
    <pre class="text-pink-300 leading-relaxed overflow-x-auto whitespace-pre-wrap">
{`$ moro dashboard --port 3000 --host 127.0.0.1

╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│   MoroAI Mission Control Dashboard v0.1.0        │
│   Web Interface:  http://localhost:3000          │
│   REST API:       http://localhost:3000/api/v1   │
│   WebSocket:      ws://localhost:3000/api/v1/ws  │
│   Storage:        SQLite (.moro/moro.db)         │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
[READY] Press Ctrl+C to stop the dashboard server.`}
    </pre>
  </div>

  <h2>Real-Time Streaming Engine (SSE & WebSockets)</h2>
  <p>
    Standard machine learning dashboards rely on aggressive REST polling (e.g. fetching <code>/status</code> every second), which introduces latency and CPU thrashing during heavy backpropagation.
  </p>
  <p>
    MoroAI Mission Control implements a dual-channel pub/sub telemetry pipe:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li>
      <strong>Server-Sent Events (SSE) (<code>/api/v1/stream</code>):</strong> Delivers unidirectional, lightweight 60Hz telemetry ticks for active training step, rolling moving-average loss, and exact VRAM allocations directly to client SVG/Canvas charts.
    </li>
    <li>
      <strong>Bi-Directional WebSocket (<code>/api/v1/ws</code>):</strong> Facilitates instant command dispatching (such as dynamic learning rate nudges, emergency pause, or manual checkpoint creation) with sub-millisecond execution roundtrips.
    </li>
  </ul>

  <h2>Core Modules in Mission Control</h2>

  <h3>1. Interactive Dataset Studio</h3>
  <p>
    Drag and drop raw <code>.jsonl</code>, <code>.csv</code>, or <code>.parquet</code> files directly into the browser. The studio immediately runs the <strong>Epistemic Data Compiler</strong> in a background worker process, rendering:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li>Interactive token length distribution histograms</li>
    <li>Positive Pointwise Mutual Information (PPMI) density curves</li>
    <li>Visual identification of protected <strong>MI Guard Landmark</strong> samples versus pruned boilerplate</li>
  </ul>

  <h3>2. Pre-Flight VRAM Simulator</h3>
  <p>
    Before starting training, operators can adjust sequence length (e.g. 1024, 2048, 4096) and LoRA rank ($r=8, 16, 32, 64$). A dynamic gauge continuously predicts peak VRAM against available GPU memory and illuminates safety thresholds (Green: Safe, Yellow: Tight, Red: OOM Inevitable).
  </p>

  <h3>3. Evaluation Comparator & Completion Diffing</h3>
  <p>
    Compare base model versus fine-tuned checkpoint completions side by side on standardized enterprise test sets. Responses are diffed token-by-token with color-coded highlighting of strict rule compliance, hallucination markers, and Wasserstein distribution drift scores.
  </p>

  <h3>4. One-Click Runtime Deployment</h3>
  <p>
    Once an evaluation gate is certified, the operator can click <strong>Deploy to Ollama</strong>. Mission Control invokes local quantization (NF4/GGUF), compiles the Modelfile, and registers the model in the local Ollama daemon without leaving the browser.
  </p>

  <h2>REST & WebSocket Integration</h2>
  <p>
    For programmatic monitoring or embedding into internal corporate portals, Mission Control exposes comprehensive endpoints:
  </p>

  <div class="not-prose my-6 overflow-x-auto">
    <table class="w-full text-xs text-left border-collapse border border-dark-800">
      <thead>
        <tr class="bg-dark-950 text-gray-300 font-mono">
          <th class="p-3 border border-dark-800">Endpoint</th>
          <th class="p-3 border border-dark-800">Method</th>
          <th class="p-3 border border-dark-800">Description</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody class="text-gray-400 font-mono">
        <tr class="border-b border-dark-800">
          <td class="p-3 text-pink-400 font-bold">/api/v1/health</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-emerald-400 font-bold">GET</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-300">Server status, connected GPU info, and database state</td>
        </tr>
        <tr class="border-b border-dark-800">
          <td class="p-3 text-pink-400 font-bold">/api/v1/runs</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-emerald-400 font-bold">GET / POST</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-300">List historical runs or launch new training job</td>
        </tr>
        <tr class="border-b border-dark-800">
          <td class="p-3 text-pink-400 font-bold">/api/v1/runs/{'{id}'}/telemetry</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-emerald-400 font-bold">GET (SSE)</td>

        </tr>

          <td class="p-3 text-cyan-400 font-bold">POST</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-300">Trigger GGUF quantization and local Ollama registration</td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>

  <div class="not-prose mt-12 pt-6 border-t border-dark-800 flex items-center justify-between">

## Document: /docs/concepts/data-compiler/

<div class="not-prose mb-8">
    <span class="text-xs font-mono font-bold text-cyan-400 uppercase tracking-wider bg-cyan-500/10 px-2.5 py-1 rounded border border-cyan-500/20 mb-3 inline-block">
      Subsystem 01
    </span>
    <h1 class="text-3xl sm:text-5xl font-black text-white tracking-tight">Epistemic Data Compiler & MI Guard</h1>
    <p class="text-gray-400 text-base mt-2">
      Information-theoretic dataset curation engineered to mathematically protect critical domain edge cases while eliminating semantic redundancy.
    </p>
  </div>

  <MiGuardSimulator client:visible />

  <h2>The Fundamental Dilemma in Domain Fine-Tuning</h2>
  <p>
    When adapting a large language model to an enterprise domain (such as customer support, legal contracts, or medical documentation), raw input data exhibits extreme semantic skew:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Boilerplate & Generic Patterns:</strong> Greetings, standard policy disclaimers, conversational pleasantries, and common phrases occur thousands of times across the dataset.</li>
    <li><strong>Critical Domain Outliers:</strong> Rare legal exceptions, edge-case troubleshooting fixes, specialized product SKU quirks, and safety caveats occur only once or twice.</li>
  </ul>
  <p>
    Traditional deduplication systems (such as MinHash or embedding cosine distance thresholds) rely on cluster density. When they prune datasets to eliminate repetition, high-density generic clusters survive, whereas low-density domain landmarks are discarded as "unrepresentative outliers." The resulting model learns to repeat pleasantries while failing at specialized domain tasks.
  </p>

  <h2>The Mutual Information (MI) Guard</h2>
  <p>
    MoroAI solves this structural dilemma by introducing the <strong>Epistemic Data Compiler</strong> with an integrated <strong>Mutual Information (MI) Guard</strong>. Instead of judging samples solely by semantic similarity, the compiler evaluates their information-theoretic contribution to the domain corpus.
  </p>

  <div class="not-prose my-6 p-5 rounded-2xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs">
    <div class="text-gray-400 border-b border-dark-800 pb-2 mb-3 flex items-center justify-between">
      <span>Information Gain Decision Logic</span>
      <span class="text-cyan-400">Compiler Core</span>
    </div>
    <pre class="text-cyan-300 leading-relaxed overflow-x-auto whitespace-pre-wrap">
{`# 1. Calculate Pointwise Mutual Information for token pairs (w1, w2)
PPMI(w1, w2) = max( 0, log2( P(w1, w2) / (P(w1) * P(w2)) ) )

# 2. Compute Resnik Information Content against domain ontology
IC(concept) = -log( P(concept) )

# 3. MI Guard Decision Policy:
if sample.is_cluster_outlier() and sample.mean_ppmi >= mi_guard_threshold:
    preserve_sample(sample, category="MI_GUARD_LANDMARK")
elif sample.is_cluster_outlier() and sample.mean_ppmi < mi_guard_threshold:
    prune_sample(sample, category="IRRELEVANT_NOISE")
else:
    dedup_sample(sample, threshold=dedup_threshold)`}
    </pre>
  </div>

  <h2>Three-Stage Compilation Pipeline</h2>
  <ol>
    <li>
      <strong>Format Ingestion & Normalization:</strong> Ingests JSONL, CSV, Parquet, or raw text directories. Messages are mapped into a unified schema <code>{`{role: "system"|"user"|"assistant", content: string}`}</code> with automatic schema validation and PII redaction.
    </li>
    <li>
      <strong>Information Density Auditing:</strong> Calculates token entropy $H(X) = -\sum P(x) \log_2 P(x)$. Samples with repetitive token spam (e.g. garbled text or low-entropy loops) are flagged for removal.
    </li>
    <li>
      <strong>Boundary Clustering & Partitioning:</strong> Samples are embedded using a local MiniLM/Qwen embedding model. Cosine similarity determines deduplication clusters, while the MI Guard tags protected boundary samples before performing deterministic 80/10/10 train/validation/test splits.
    </li>
  </ol>

  <h2>CLI Usage & Pipeline Flags</h2>
  <p>
    Compile raw conversational logs into a hardened, balanced dataset ready for training:
  </p>

  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300">
# Ingest and compile dataset with MI Guard enabled
moro data build \
    --source ./data/customer_support_raw.jsonl \
    --mi-guard-threshold 0.85 \
    --dedup-threshold 0.88 \
    --output ./data/compiled/

# Inspect information-theoretic balance and token distribution
moro data report --compiled-dir ./data/compiled/
  </pre>

  <h2>Comparison: Naive Deduplication vs MoroAI MI Guard</h2>
  <div class="not-prose my-6 overflow-x-auto">
    <table class="w-full text-xs text-left border-collapse border border-dark-800">
      <thead>
        <tr class="bg-dark-950 text-gray-300 font-mono">
          <th class="p-3 border border-dark-800">Metric / Capability</th>
          <th class="p-3 border border-dark-800">Naive MinHash / Cosine</th>
          <th class="p-3 border border-dark-800 text-cyan-400">MoroAI Epistemic Compiler</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody class="text-gray-400 font-mono">
        <tr class="border-b border-dark-800">
          <td class="p-3 text-white">Rare Domain Fact Retention</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-red-400">~18% (Discarded as outliers)</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-emerald-400 font-bold">&gt;99.2% (MI Guard Protected)</td>
        </tr>
        <tr class="border-b border-dark-800">
          <td class="p-3 text-white">Boilerplate Pruning</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-yellow-400">Partial (Threshold dependent)</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-emerald-400 font-bold">Comprehensive Entropy Gated</td>
        </tr>
        <tr class="border-b border-dark-800">
          <td class="p-3 text-white">Cryptographic Lineage</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-red-400">None</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-emerald-400 font-bold">SHA-256 Digest in SBOM</td>
        </tr>
        <tr class="border-b border-dark-800">
          <td class="p-3 text-white">PII Pre-Scanning</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-red-400">Manual / External</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-emerald-400 font-bold">Built-In Automatic Regex + NLP</td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>

  <div class="not-prose mt-12 pt-6 border-t border-dark-800 flex items-center justify-between">
    <a href="/docs/concepts/overview/" class="text-xs font-semibold text-gray-400 hover:text-white transition-colors">
      ← Architecture Overview
    </a>
    <a href="/docs/concepts/ppci-filtering/" class="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-5 py-2.5 rounded-xl bg-moro-500 hover:bg-moro-400 text-white font-semibold text-xs transition-colors">
      <span>PPMI & Information Content</span>
      <ArrowRight class="w-3.5 h-3.5" />

## Document: /docs/concepts/drift-detection/

<div class="not-prose mb-8">
    <span class="text-xs font-mono font-bold text-moro-400 uppercase tracking-wider bg-moro-500/10 px-2.5 py-1 rounded border border-moro-500/20 mb-3 inline-block">
      Safety & Alignment
    </span>
    <h1 class="text-3xl sm:text-5xl font-black text-white tracking-tight">Statistical Drift Detection</h1>
    <p class="text-gray-400 text-base mt-2">
      Preventing catastrophic forgetting and semantic drift during local fine-tuning cycles.
    </p>
  </div>

  <h2>Why Drift Detection is Essential</h2>
  <p>
    When adapting a base model to a narrow domain, there is high risk of catastrophic forgetting—the model degrades in general reasoning or shifts too drastically in its token probabilities. MoroAI computes three mathematical drift metrics between the base model and adapted candidate:
  </p>

  <ul>
    <li><strong>Wasserstein Distance (Earth Mover's Distance):</strong> Measures the minimum work required to transform the output token probability distribution into the base distribution.</li>
    <li><strong>Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD):</strong> Symmetrical bound quantifying distribution divergence.</li>
    <li><strong>Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD):</strong> Measures distance between embedding representations in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS).</li>
  </ul>

  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300">
{`# Certified safety gate requires Wasserstein drift < 0.05
moro eval drift --run-id run_01 --threshold 0.05`}
  </pre>

  <div class="not-prose mt-12 pt-6 border-t border-dark-800 flex items-center justify-between">
    <a href="/docs/concepts/eval-harness/" class="text-xs font-semibold text-gray-400 hover:text-white transition-colors">
      ← Eval Harness
    </a>
    <a href="/docs/concepts/flywheel/" class="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-5 py-2.5 rounded-xl bg-moro-500 hover:bg-moro-400 text-white font-semibold text-xs transition-colors">
      <span>DPO Flywheel</span>
      <ArrowRight class="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
    </a>
  </div>

## Document: /docs/concepts/eval-harness/

<div class="not-prose mb-8">
    <span class="text-xs font-mono font-bold text-red-400 uppercase tracking-wider bg-red-500/10 px-2.5 py-1 rounded border border-red-500/20 mb-3 inline-block">
      Subsystem 04
    </span>
    <h1 class="text-3xl sm:text-5xl font-black text-white tracking-tight">Multi-Layer Evaluation Harness</h1>
    <p class="text-gray-400 text-base mt-2">
      Comprehensive model certification across deterministic rules, semantic judges, distribution drift detection, and adversarial stress tests.
    </p>
  </div>

  <h2>Beyond Validation Loss: The Need for Multi-Layer Certification</h2>
  <p>
    In academic research, evaluation often stops at cross-entropy validation loss or standard perplexity. However, in enterprise deployment, an adapted model with a low validation loss can still:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li>Violate strict JSON schema requirements, producing malformed API payloads</li>
    <li>Hallucinate plausible-sounding legal or medical falsehoods</li>
    <li>Experience <strong>catastrophic forgetting</strong> of general reasoning capabilities</li>
    <li>Break under noisy user input with misspellings or colloquial phrasing</li>
  </ul>
  <p>
    MoroAI enforces four distinct evaluation gates before certifying any checkpoint for production release.
  </p>

  <h2>The 4-Layer Validation Gates</h2>

  <div class="space-y-4 not-prose my-6 text-sm">
    <div class="p-4 rounded-xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800">
      <div class="flex items-center justify-between mb-1">
        <span class="text-red-400 font-bold font-mono">Layer 1: Deterministic Syntax & Schema Gates</span>
        <span class="text-xs font-mono text-gray-500">Weight: 100% Mandatory</span>
      </div>
      <p class="text-gray-300 text-xs leading-relaxed">
        Validates completions against strict deterministic patterns. Checks include exact JSON Schema validation, regex constraints for mandatory IDs or formatting, and zero-tolerance scans for forbidden tokens or hallucinated URLs.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="p-4 rounded-xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800">
      <div class="flex items-center justify-between mb-1">
        <span class="text-red-400 font-bold font-mono">Layer 2: Semantic LLM Domain Judge</span>
        <span class="text-xs font-mono text-gray-500">Weight: Accuracy Benchmark</span>
      </div>
      <p class="text-gray-300 text-xs leading-relaxed">
        Executes reference-guided domain evaluation against ground-truth question-answer pairs. An evaluator model scores factual correctness, reasoning completeness, and tone fidelity on a calibrated 1-5 scale using structured JSON rubrics.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="p-4 rounded-xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800">
      <div class="flex items-center justify-between mb-1">
        <span class="text-red-400 font-bold font-mono">Layer 3: Wasserstein Embedding Drift Detection</span>
        <span class="text-xs font-mono text-gray-500">Weight: General Reasoning Guard</span>
      </div>
      <p class="text-gray-300 text-xs leading-relaxed">
        Calculates the Earth Mover's (Wasserstein-1) distance between output embedding representations of the fine-tuned model versus the base foundation model on standard anchor prompts. If drift exceeds $W_1 > 0.05$, the model is flagged for catastrophic forgetting.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="p-4 rounded-xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800">
      <div class="flex items-center justify-between mb-1">
        <span class="text-red-400 font-bold font-mono">Layer 4: Adversarial Perturbation Stress Testing</span>
        <span class="text-xs font-mono text-gray-500">Weight: Robustness Guard</span>
      </div>
      <p class="text-gray-300 text-xs leading-relaxed">
        Automatically injects synthetic perturbations into test prompts (character swaps, common keyboard typos, and homoglyphs). The harness verifies that the model's structured completion remains invariant under realistic noisy operator input.
      </p>
    </div>
  </div>

  <h2>Defining an Evaluation Suite (eval_suite.yaml)</h2>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300 leading-relaxed">
name: "customer-support-eval"
version: "1.0.0"
gates:
  deterministic:
    min_pass_rate: 1.0        # 100% must pass JSON schema
  semantic:
    min_accuracy: 0.90         # 90% domain accuracy
  drift:
    max_wasserstein: 0.05      # No severe representation collapse
  adversarial:
    min_stability: 0.85        # Robust against typos

tests:
  - id: "test_refund_json"
    prompt: "Customer requests refund for order #12345 after 14 days."
    expected_schema:
      type: "object"
      required: ["eligible", "refund_amount", "reason_code"]
    forbidden_terms: ["I think", "maybe", "as an AI"]
  </pre>

  <h2>Running Evaluations via CLI</h2>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-orange-300">
# Run complete evaluation harness against candidate checkpoint
moro eval run --checkpoint ./runs/run_01/checkpoints/best/ --suite ./eval/eval_suite.yaml

# Compare candidate checkpoint against base foundation model
moro eval compare --base Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B --candidate ./runs/run_01/checkpoints/best/
  </pre>

  <div class="not-prose mt-12 pt-6 border-t border-dark-800 flex items-center justify-between">
    <a href="/docs/concepts/training-engine/" class="text-xs font-semibold text-gray-400 hover:text-white transition-colors">
      ← Self-Healing Training Engine
    </a>
    <a href="/docs/concepts/drift-detection/" class="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-5 py-2.5 rounded-xl bg-moro-500 hover:bg-moro-400 text-white font-semibold text-xs transition-colors">
      <span>Statistical Drift Detection</span>
      <ArrowRight class="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
    </a>
  </div>

## Document: /docs/concepts/flywheel/

<div class="not-prose mb-8">
    <span class="text-xs font-mono font-bold text-amber-400 uppercase tracking-wider bg-amber-500/10 px-2.5 py-1 rounded border border-amber-500/20 mb-3 inline-block">
      Subsystem 05
    </span>
    <h1 class="text-3xl sm:text-5xl font-black text-white tracking-tight">Closed-Loop DPO Feedback Flywheel</h1>
    <p class="text-gray-400 text-base mt-2">
      Transforming live production interactions and human operator edits into preference pairs for continuous local model alignment.
    </p>
  </div>

  <h2>Why Static Models Degrade Over Time</h2>
  <p>
    When a model is fine-tuned and deployed into an enterprise environment, its real-world performance is tested by evolving edge cases, novel customer questions, and shifting operational terminology. In typical cloud-based setups, closing this loop requires shipping sensitive conversation transcripts to external annotation vendors.
  </p>
  <p>
    MoroAI creates a <strong>local, sovereign learning flywheel</strong>. Human operators naturally correct model answers or submit thumbs-up / thumbs-down ratings during daily operations. The MoroAI Flywheel mines these local signals and formats them into high-signal <strong>Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)</strong> datasets without data ever leaving the workstation or VPC.
  </p>

  <h2>Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) Mechanics</h2>
  <p>
    Traditional RLHF requires training a separate reward model followed by complex PPO reinforcement learning, which is notoriously unstable and memory-intensive on consumer GPUs. DPO optimizes the policy model directly on preference pairs using the exact analytical relationship between policy and reward:
  </p>

  <div class="not-prose my-6 p-5 rounded-2xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs">
    <div class="text-gray-400 border-b border-dark-800 pb-2 mb-3 flex items-center justify-between">
      <span>DPO Closed-Form Objective</span>
      <span class="text-amber-400">Optimization Math</span>
    </div>
    <pre class="text-amber-300 leading-relaxed overflow-x-auto whitespace-pre-wrap">
{`L_DPO(π_θ; π_ref) = -E_(x, y_w, y_l) [
    log σ( β * log( π_θ(y_w | x) / π_ref(y_w | x) ) - β * log( π_θ(y_l | x) / π_ref(y_l | x) ) )
]

Where:
  x     = The user prompt
  y_w   = Chosen response (human operator edit or high-rated completion)
  y_l   = Rejected response (original unedited model completion)
  π_ref = Frozen reference model (initial fine-tuned LoRA checkpoint)
  β     = Temperature hyperparameter controlling deviation penalty (default 0.1)`}
    </pre>
  </div>

  <h2>The 4-Step Flywheel Lifecycle</h2>
  <ol>
    <li>
      <strong>Local Interaction Logging:</strong> As queries pass through the local Ollama or vLLM proxy, input prompts and completions are securely persisted to local encrypted SQLite storage (<code>.moro/moro.db</code>).
    </li>
    <li>
      <strong>Preference Pair Extraction:</strong> When an operator manually corrects an output in Mission Control or an integrated CRM, the engine constructs a preference pair with the corrected text as <code>chosen</code> and the initial output as <code>rejected</code>.
    </li>
    <li>
      <strong>Confidence Margin Filtering:</strong> To eliminate ambiguous feedback, pairs where the operator edit is merely trivial whitespace or where rating confidence is below $\Delta = 0.3$ are automatically pruned.
    </li>
    <li>
      <strong>Automated Offline Alignment:</strong> When a user-configured threshold of validated pairs is reached (e.g. 250 pairs), the engine schedules an automated overnight DPO alignment run, verifies the model against the evaluation harness, and generates a new versioned release candidate.
    </li>
  </ol>

  <h2>CLI Mining & Alignment Commands</h2>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-amber-300 leading-relaxed">
# Mine interaction logs for high-confidence preference pairs
moro flywheel process \
    --interactions ./logs/chat_ops.jsonl \
    --min-margin 0.3 \
    --output ./data/dpo_pairs.jsonl

# Execute local DPO fine-tuning alignment round
moro flywheel align \
    --base-checkpoint ./runs/run_01/checkpoints/best/ \
    --pairs ./data/dpo_pairs.jsonl \
    --beta 0.1 \
    --output ./runs/dpo_aligned/
  </pre>

  <div class="not-prose mt-12 pt-6 border-t border-dark-800 flex items-center justify-between">
    <a href="/docs/concepts/eval-harness/" class="text-xs font-semibold text-gray-400 hover:text-white transition-colors">
      ← Multi-Layer Eval Harness
    </a>
    <a href="/docs/concepts/dashboard/" class="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-5 py-2.5 rounded-xl bg-moro-500 hover:bg-moro-400 text-white font-semibold text-xs transition-colors">
      <span>Mission Control UI</span>
      <ArrowRight class="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
    </a>
  </div>

## Document: /docs/concepts/governance/

<div class="not-prose mb-8">
    <span class="text-xs font-mono font-bold text-moro-400 uppercase tracking-wider bg-moro-500/10 px-2.5 py-1 rounded border border-moro-500/20 mb-3 inline-block">
      Compliance & Audit
    </span>
    <h1 class="text-3xl sm:text-5xl font-black text-white tracking-tight">Release Governance & Cryptographic SBOM</h1>
    <p class="text-gray-400 text-base mt-2">
      Auditable model provenance binding data, recipes, evaluations, and weights into an immutable Software Bill of Materials.
    </p>
  </div>

  <h2>Cryptographic Bill of Materials (SBOM)</h2>
  <p>
    Regulated industries cannot deploy black-box models without proof of training lineage. MoroAI automatically generates a signed JSON manifest for every release candidate:
  </p>

  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-teal-300">
{`{
  "release_id": "rel_2026_09_28_01",
  "model_name": "moro-enterprise:v1.0.0",
  "provenance": {
    "dataset_sha256": "8f3b2049e0c19a0a...",
    "recipe_sha256": "44ea1041b8a9018f...",
    "base_model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B",
    "checkpoint_sha256": "d9810a9c72e19a0f..."
  },
  "evaluation_gate": {
    "passed": true,
    "deterministic_rule_pass_rate": 1.0,
    "drift_score_wasserstein": 0.021,
    "eval_signature": "sig_rsa4096_d892a01"
  }
}`}
  </pre>

  <h2>Verifying a Model</h2>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300">
moro release verify --release-id rel_2026_09_28_01
  </pre>

  <div class="not-prose mt-12 pt-6 border-t border-dark-800 flex items-center justify-between">
    <a href="/docs/concepts/flywheel/" class="text-xs font-semibold text-gray-400 hover:text-white transition-colors">
      ← DPO Flywheel
    </a>
    <a href="/docs/cookbook/" class="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-5 py-2.5 rounded-xl bg-moro-500 hover:bg-moro-400 text-white font-semibold text-xs transition-colors">
      <span>Cookbook Overview</span>
      <ArrowRight class="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
    </a>
  </div>

## Document: /docs/concepts/lineage-graphs/

<div class="not-prose mb-8">
    <span class="text-xs font-mono font-bold text-moro-400 uppercase tracking-wider bg-moro-500/10 px-2.5 py-1 rounded border border-moro-500/20 mb-3 inline-block">
      Provenance & Audit
    </span>
    <h1 class="text-3xl sm:text-5xl font-black text-white tracking-tight">Lineage Graphs: Complete Provenance Tracking</h1>
    <p class="text-gray-400 text-base mt-2">
      Immutable lifecycle tracking from raw input documents to deployed local model weights using an embedded Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG).
    </p>
  </div>

  <h2>The Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)</h2>
  <p>
    In high-compliance deployments, knowing what data a model was trained on is mandatory. MoroAI maintains an embedded graph ledger (stored in <code>.moro/moro.db</code>) where every entity is a cryptographic node linked by directional edges:
  </p>

  <div class="not-prose my-6 p-5 rounded-2xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs">
    <div class="text-gray-400 border-b border-dark-800 pb-2 mb-3 flex items-center justify-between">
      <span>End-to-End Provenance Graph</span>
      <span class="text-moro-400">Node & Edge Lifecycle</span>
    </div>
    <pre class="text-sky-300 leading-relaxed overflow-x-auto whitespace-pre-wrap">
{`raw_source:pharma_docs.jsonl (sha256: 8f3b20...a19c)
    │
    ▼ [DERIVED_FROM]
dataset_version:pharma_v1 (1,247 curated samples)
    │
    ▼ [TRAINED_ON]
training_run:run_123456 (LoRA r=16, alpha=32, Qwen2.5-1.5B)
    │
    ▼ [EVALUATED_BY]
eval_result:eval_789 (Deterministic: 100%, Semantic: 94.2%)
    │
    ▼ [RELEASED_FROM]
release:v1.0.0 (GGUF Q4_K_M + signed SBOM)
    │
    ▼ [DEPLOYED_TO]
deployment:ollama_pharma_v1 (http://localhost:11434)
    │
    ▼ [FEEDBACK_FOR]
feedback_batch:batch_001 (342 human operator edits)
    │
    ▼ [ALIGNED_BY]
dpo_epoch:epoch_001 (continuous local refinement)`}
    </pre>
  </div>

  <h2>Querying Lineage Programmatically</h2>
  <p>
    The MoroAI Python SDK allows engineers to trace artifacts backwards or forwards across the graph:
  </p>

  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-emerald-300 leading-relaxed">
{`from pathlib import Path
from moro.state.manager import StateManager
from moro.state.models import EdgeType

# Initialize state manager pointing to local database
state = StateManager(Path(".moro/moro.db"))

# 1. Trace the complete ancestral lineage of an active deployment:
lineage = state.trace_lineage("deployment_ollama_pharma_v1")
print("Trained from raw files:", lineage.root_sources)
print("Cryptographic dataset hash:", lineage.dataset_sha256)

# 2. Find all models derived from a specific dataset version:
runs = state.get_connected_nodes(
    "dataset_pharma_v1",
    edge_type=EdgeType.TRAINED_ON,
    direction="outgoing"
)
for run in runs:
    print(f"Run {run.id}: Validation Loss = {run.metrics.val_loss}")`}
  </pre>

  <h2>Lineage in Mission Control Dashboard</h2>
  <p>
    When using the Mission Control UI (<code>moro dashboard</code>), lineage graphs are rendered as interactive node-link diagrams. Operators can click any model checkpoint, view its exact dataset origin, inspect evaluation certificates, and verify cryptographic hashes with a single click.
  </p>

  <div class="not-prose mt-12 pt-6 border-t border-dark-800 flex items-center justify-between">
    <a href="/docs/concepts/ppci-filtering/" class="text-xs font-semibold text-gray-400 hover:text-white transition-colors">
      ← PPMI Filtering
    </a>
    <a href="/docs/concepts/recipe-engine/" class="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-5 py-2.5 rounded-xl bg-moro-500 hover:bg-moro-400 text-white font-semibold text-xs transition-colors">
      <span>VRAM Recipe Engine</span>
      <ArrowRight class="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
    </a>
  </div>

## Document: /docs/concepts/overview/

<div class="not-prose mb-8">
    <span class="text-xs font-mono font-bold text-moro-400 uppercase tracking-wider bg-moro-500/10 px-2.5 py-1 rounded border border-moro-500/20 mb-3 inline-block">
      Architecture
    </span>
    <h1 class="text-3xl sm:text-5xl font-black text-white tracking-tight">System Architecture Overview</h1>
    <p class="text-gray-400 text-base mt-2">
      How MoroAI's six core architectural subsystems assemble into a closed-loop local model adaptation foundry.
    </p>
  </div>

  <h2>Architectural Layers</h2>
  <p>
    MoroAI is designed as an integrated six-layer pipeline that transforms raw unstructured data into deployed, continuously self-improving local models:
  </p>

  <div class="not-prose space-y-4 my-8">
    <div class="p-5 rounded-2xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800 flex items-start gap-4">
      <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-xl bg-blue-500/10 border border-blue-500/20 flex items-center justify-center text-blue-400 shrink-0">
        <Database class="w-5 h-5" />
      </div>
      <div>
        <h4 class="text-base font-bold text-white mb-1">1. Epistemic Data Layer</h4>
        <p class="text-xs text-gray-400 leading-relaxed">
          Ingests raw CSV, JSONL, and text documents. Applies Positive Pointwise Mutual Information (PPMI), Resnik Information Content, and the MI Guard to retain critical domain corner cases while eliminating redundancy.
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="p-5 rounded-2xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800 flex items-start gap-4">
      <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-xl bg-emerald-500/10 border border-emerald-500/20 flex items-center justify-center text-emerald-400 shrink-0">
        <Cpu class="w-5 h-5" />
      </div>
      <div>
        <h4 class="text-base font-bold text-white mb-1">2. Hardware-Aware Recipe Layer</h4>
        <p class="text-xs text-gray-400 leading-relaxed">
          Probes local GPU architecture (CUDA, Apple Silicon Metal, ROCm). Mathematically computes activation memory and parameter gradients to output a zero-OOM <code>moro.yaml</code> recipe.
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="p-5 rounded-2xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800 flex items-start gap-4">
      <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-xl bg-purple-500/10 border border-purple-500/20 flex items-center justify-center text-purple-400 shrink-0">
        <Zap class="w-5 h-5" />
      </div>
      <div>
        <h4 class="text-base font-bold text-white mb-1">3. Self-Healing Execution Layer</h4>
        <p class="text-xs text-gray-400 leading-relaxed">
          Executes QLoRA / LoRA fine-tuning under an active supervisor. Catches CUDA memory limits and loss spikes with a 5-step autonomous recovery sequence.
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="p-5 rounded-2xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800 flex items-start gap-4">
      <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-xl bg-red-500/10 border border-red-500/20 flex items-center justify-center text-red-400 shrink-0">
        <Shield class="w-5 h-5" />
      </div>
      <div>
        <h4 class="text-base font-bold text-white mb-1">4. Multi-Layer Evaluation Layer</h4>
        <p class="text-xs text-gray-400 leading-relaxed">
          Tests checkpoints across deterministic schema constraints, semantic LLM accuracy, Wasserstein distribution drift, and adversarial perturbation invariance.
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="p-5 rounded-2xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800 flex items-start gap-4">
      <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-xl bg-indigo-500/10 border border-indigo-500/20 flex items-center justify-center text-indigo-400 shrink-0">
        <Rocket class="w-5 h-5" />
      </div>
      <div>
        <h4 class="text-base font-bold text-white mb-1">5. Release Governance & Serving Layer</h4>
        <p class="text-xs text-gray-400 leading-relaxed">
          Quantizes weights to GGUF (Q4_K_M/Q8_0), signs cryptographic SHA-256 SBOM provenance records, and injects Modelfiles directly into local Ollama or vLLM engines.
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="p-5 rounded-2xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800 flex items-start gap-4">
      <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-xl bg-amber-500/10 border border-amber-500/20 flex items-center justify-center text-amber-400 shrink-0">
        <RefreshCcw class="w-5 h-5" />
      </div>
      <div>
        <h4 class="text-base font-bold text-white mb-1">6. DPO Continuous Alignment Layer</h4>
        <p class="text-xs text-gray-400 leading-relaxed">
          Mines real-world user interactions and feedback logs for chosen/rejected preference pairs to trigger offline alignment loops.
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <h2>State Management & Lineage DAG</h2>
  <p>
    All operations are tracked in a local SQLite database (<code>.moro/state.db</code>) modeled as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG). Every deployed model can be audited backward to the exact data lines, token entropy, hyperparameter seeds, and hardware profile used in its creation.
  </p>

  <div class="not-prose mt-12 pt-6 border-t border-dark-800 flex items-center justify-between">

## Document: /docs/concepts/ppci-filtering/

<div class="not-prose mb-8">
    <span class="text-xs font-mono font-bold text-cyan-400 uppercase tracking-wider bg-cyan-500/10 px-2.5 py-1 rounded border border-cyan-500/20 mb-3 inline-block">
      Information Theory
    </span>
    <h1 class="text-3xl sm:text-5xl font-black text-white tracking-tight">PPMI Filtering: The Mathematics of Domain Relevance</h1>
    <p class="text-gray-400 text-base mt-2">
      How Positive Pointwise Mutual Information quantifies semantic association strength and protects critical domain landmarks from deletion.
    </p>
  </div>

  <h2>What is PPMI?</h2>
  <p>
    Positive Pointwise Mutual Information (PPMI) measures the statistical association strength between a token $w$ and a target enterprise domain $D$:
  </p>

  <div class="not-prose my-6 p-5 rounded-2xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs">
    <div class="text-gray-400 border-b border-dark-800 pb-2 mb-3 flex items-center justify-between">
      <span>Formal Mathematical Definition</span>
      <span class="text-cyan-400">PPMI Equation</span>
    </div>
    <pre class="text-cyan-300 leading-relaxed overflow-x-auto whitespace-pre-wrap">
{`PPMI(w, D) = max( 0, log2( P(w, D) / ( P(w) * P(D) ) ) )

Where:
  P(w, D) = Probability of token w occurring within the domain dataset D
  P(w)    = Marginal probability of token w in a standard general English corpus
  P(D)    = Prior probability of the domain subset`}
    </pre>
  </div>

  <h2>Intuition: General vs Domain Specific Vocabulary</h2>
  <p>
    Tokens that occur uniformly across all natural language receive a PPMI close to zero, whereas terminology that clusters specifically inside your enterprise dataset receives a high score:
  </p>

  <div class="not-prose my-6 overflow-x-auto">
    <table class="w-full text-xs text-left border-collapse border border-dark-800">
      <thead>
        <tr class="bg-dark-950 text-gray-300 font-mono">
          <th class="p-3 border border-dark-800">Token ($w$)</th>
          <th class="p-3 border border-dark-800">PPMI (Medical Domain)</th>
          <th class="p-3 border border-dark-800">PPMI (Legal Domain)</th>
          <th class="p-3 border border-dark-800">Information Interpretation</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody class="text-gray-400 font-mono">
        <tr class="border-b border-dark-800">
          <td class="p-3 text-white font-bold">pharmacokinetics</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-emerald-400 font-bold">8.42</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-500">0.00</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-300">Strong medical landmark token</td>
        </tr>
        <tr class="border-b border-dark-800">
          <td class="p-3 text-white font-bold">indemnification</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-500">0.12</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-emerald-400 font-bold">7.89</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-300">Strong legal landmark token</td>
        </tr>
        <tr class="border-b border-dark-800">
          <td class="p-3 text-white font-bold">the / is / and</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-500">0.00</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-500">0.00</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-300">Generic stop words (uninformative)</td>
        </tr>
        <tr class="border-b border-dark-800">
          <td class="p-3 text-white font-bold">bioequivalence</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-emerald-400 font-bold">6.91</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-500">0.05</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-300">High informational density</td>
        </tr>
        <tr class="border-b border-dark-800">
          <td class="p-3 text-white font-bold">jurisdiction</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-500">0.24</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-emerald-400 font-bold">6.75</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-300">High legal specificity</td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>

  <h2>Python Reference Implementation</h2>
  <p>
    Below is the algorithmic core utilized inside <code>moro.data.compiler</code> to score token distributions:
  </p>

  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300 leading-relaxed">
import numpy as np
from collections import Counter

def calculate_ppmi(
    domain_tokens: Counter,
    general_tokens: Counter,
    total_domain: int,
    total_general: int,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Calculate Positive Pointwise Mutual Information for domain vocabulary."""
    ppmi_scores = {}

    for token, domain_count in domain_tokens.items():
        # Probability of token within enterprise domain:
        p_w_domain = domain_count / total_domain

        # Background probability across general corpus:
        general_count = general_tokens.get(token, 1)
        p_w_general = general_count / total_general

        # Calculate Pointwise Mutual Information:
        pmi = np.log2(p_w_domain / p_w_general)
        ppmi_scores[token] = float(max(0.0, pmi))

    return ppmi_scores
  </pre>

  <h2>Tuning PPMI Thresholds in moro.yaml</h2>
  <p>Customize the sensitivity of the MI Guard inside your configuration:</p>

  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-emerald-300">
dataset:
  source: ./data/raw/contracts.jsonl
  # Minimum PPMI for a sample to be marked domain-relevant:
  min_ppmi: 1.0

  # PPMI threshold required to trigger an MI Guard override on rare clusters:
  mi_guard_ppmi_threshold: 2.0
  </pre>

  <div class="not-prose mt-12 pt-6 border-t border-dark-800 flex items-center justify-between">
    <a href="/docs/concepts/data-compiler/" class="text-xs font-semibold text-gray-400 hover:text-white transition-colors">
      ← Epistemic Data Compiler
    </a>
    <a href="/docs/concepts/lineage-graphs/" class="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-5 py-2.5 rounded-xl bg-moro-500 hover:bg-moro-400 text-white font-semibold text-xs transition-colors">
      <span>Lineage Graphs</span>
      <ArrowRight class="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
    </a>
  </div>

## Document: /docs/concepts/recipe-engine/

<div class="not-prose mb-8">
    <span class="text-xs font-mono font-bold text-emerald-400 uppercase tracking-wider bg-emerald-500/10 px-2.5 py-1 rounded border border-emerald-500/20 mb-3 inline-block">
      Subsystem 02
    </span>
    <h1 class="text-3xl sm:text-5xl font-black text-white tracking-tight">VRAM Recipe Predictor</h1>
    <p class="text-gray-400 text-base mt-2">
      Eliminating trial-and-error fine-tuning by simulating memory consumption down to the megabyte before touching GPU memory.
    </p>
  </div>

  <VramCalculator client:visible />

  <h2>The VRAM Memory Formula</h2>
  <p>
    When fine-tuning on consumer hardware, memory exhaustion is non-linear. Peak GPU VRAM is modeled prior to training execution across five critical tensor allocations:
  </p>

  <div class="not-prose my-6 p-5 rounded-2xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs">
    <div class="text-gray-400 border-b border-dark-800 pb-2 mb-3 flex items-center justify-between">
      <span>Analytical VRAM Memory Model</span>
      <span class="text-emerald-400">Peak Memory Equation</span>
    </div>
    <pre class="text-emerald-300 leading-relaxed overflow-x-auto whitespace-pre-wrap">
{`VRAM_Peak = M_base + M_lora + M_optimizer + M_activations + M_cuda_context

Where:
  M_base        = (N_params * B_quant) / 8           # Base weights in NF4 / FP16
  M_lora        = 2 * rank * d_model * N_targets * 4 # Trainable LoRA adapter matrices (FP32)
  M_optimizer   = M_lora * 2                         # 8-bit AdamW first and second moments
  M_activations = b * s * L * (34 * d_model + 5 * s * h) # Backprop activation tensors
  M_cuda_ctx    = ~850MB to 1.2GB                     # CUDA driver context & kernels`}
    </pre>
  </div>

  <h2>Hardware Tier Presets & Validation</h2>
  <p>
    The engine maintains validated memory envelopes across standard consumer and workstation GPUs:
  </p>

  <div class="not-prose my-6 overflow-x-auto">
    <table class="w-full text-xs text-left border-collapse border border-dark-800">
      <thead>
        <tr class="bg-dark-950 text-gray-300 font-mono">
          <th class="p-3 border border-dark-800">Hardware Profile</th>
          <th class="p-3 border border-dark-800">Available Memory</th>
          <th class="p-3 border border-dark-800">Recommended Model</th>
          <th class="p-3 border border-dark-800">LoRA Rank (r)</th>
          <th class="p-3 border border-dark-800">Context Length</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody class="text-gray-400 font-mono">
        <tr class="border-b border-dark-800">
          <td class="p-3 text-white font-bold">RTX 3060 / 4060</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-emerald-400">12 GB VRAM</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-300">Qwen2.5-1.5B / Llama-3.2-1B</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-300">r=16, alpha=32</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-cyan-400">2,048 tokens</td>
        </tr>
        <tr class="border-b border-dark-800">
          <td class="p-3 text-white font-bold">RTX 4070 / 4070 Ti</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-emerald-400">12–16 GB VRAM</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-300">Qwen2.5-3B / Llama-3.2-3B</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-300">r=32, alpha=64</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-cyan-400">4,096 tokens</td>
        </tr>
        <tr class="border-b border-dark-800">
          <td class="p-3 text-white font-bold">RTX 3090 / 4090</td>

          <td class="p-3 text-emerald-400">16–64 GB Unified</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-300">Qwen2.5-7B / Mistral-7B</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-300">r=16, alpha=32</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-cyan-400">2,048 tokens</td>
        </tr>
        <tr class="border-b border-dark-800">
          <td class="p-3 text-white font-bold">Cloud A100 / H100</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-emerald-400">80 GB VRAM</td>
          <td class="p-3 text-gray-300">Qwen2.5-14B / 32B</td>

        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>

  <h2>Generating a Reproducible Recipe</h2>
  <p>
    Run the recipe engine to automatically probe your active GPU driver, detect memory bandwidth, and output a guaranteed zero-OOM <code>moro.yaml</code> configuration:
  </p>

  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-emerald-300">
# Automatically audit GPU and generate optimal training configuration
moro recipe generate --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B --hardware detect --output ./moro.yaml
  </pre>

  <h2>Generated Recipe File Anatomy (moro.yaml)</h2>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300">
name: "customer-support-qwen"
version: "0.1.0"
model:
  base: "Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B"
  quantization: "nf4"        # 4-bit NormalFloat quantization
  lora_rank: 16
  lora_alpha: 32
  lora_dropout: 0.05
  target_modules: ["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj", "o_proj", "gate_proj", "up_proj", "down_proj"]

training:
  micro_batch_size: 2
  gradient_accumulation_steps: 8
  learning_rate: 2.0e-4
  max_seq_length: 2048
  optimizer: "adamw_8bit"
  gradient_checkpointing: true
  auto_heal: true            # Enables 5-level autonomous OOM recovery
  </pre>

  <div class="not-prose mt-12 pt-6 border-t border-dark-800 flex items-center justify-between">
    <a href="/docs/concepts/lineage-graphs/" class="text-xs font-semibold text-gray-400 hover:text-white transition-colors">
      ← Lineage Graphs
    </a>
    <a href="/docs/concepts/training-engine/" class="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-5 py-2.5 rounded-xl bg-moro-500 hover:bg-moro-400 text-white font-semibold text-xs transition-colors">
      <span>Self-Healing Engine</span>
      <ArrowRight class="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
    </a>
  </div>

---

## Document: /docs/concepts/training-engine/

<div class="not-prose mb-8">
    <span class="text-xs font-mono font-bold text-purple-400 uppercase tracking-wider bg-purple-500/10 px-2.5 py-1 rounded border border-purple-500/20 mb-3 inline-block">
      Subsystem 03
    </span>
    <h1 class="text-3xl sm:text-5xl font-black text-white tracking-tight">OOM Auto-Recovery & Self-Healing Engine</h1>
    <p class="text-gray-400 text-base mt-2">
      Zero-loss training recovery that intercepts CUDA out-of-memory errors and loss explosions in-flight without aborting the run.
    </p>
  </div>

  <h2>Why Unattended Local Training Fails</h2>
  <p>
    Machine learning fine-tuning jobs on consumer GPUs are inherently fragile. Even when pre-flight estimates indicate safe headroom, two runtime anomalies routinely terminate processes:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li>
      <strong>Burst Sequence Outliers (CUDA OOM):</strong> A mini-batch containing conversations with outlier token lengths (e.g. 3,800 tokens instead of the mean 1,200 tokens) causes quadratic attention memory consumption ($O(N^2)$), instantly crashing the PyTorch allocator.
    </li>
    <li>
      <strong>Gradient Explosion / NaN Divergence:</strong> Mixed-precision (FP16/BF16) training on small datasets occasionally encounters extreme gradient norms, causing weights to turn into NaNs or training loss to spike by &gt;300%.
    </li>
  </ul>

  <h2>The 5-Level Autonomous Escalation Ladder</h2>
  <p>
    MoroAI replaces the standard unhandled exception loop with a progressive <strong>Autonomous Healer Protocol</strong>. When an anomaly occurs, the engine intercepts the signal and executes the lowest-impact resolution:
  </p>

  <div class="space-y-4 not-prose my-6 text-sm">
    <div class="p-4 rounded-xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800">
      <div class="flex items-center justify-between mb-1">
        <span class="text-purple-400 font-bold font-mono">Level 1: Allocator Cache Evacuation</span>
        <span class="text-xs font-mono text-gray-500">Latency: ~400ms</span>
      </div>
      <p class="text-gray-300 text-xs leading-relaxed">
        Invokes <code>torch.cuda.empty_cache()</code> and forces Python cyclic garbage collection. This defragments the CUDA memory allocator, reclaiming up to 1.5GB of stale buffer blocks without altering training state.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="p-4 rounded-xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800">
      <div class="flex items-center justify-between mb-1">
        <span class="text-purple-400 font-bold font-mono">Level 2: Dynamic Micro-Batch Halving</span>
        <span class="text-xs font-mono text-gray-500">Mathematical Gradient Equivalence</span>
      </div>
      <p class="text-gray-300 text-xs leading-relaxed">
        Divides the per-device micro-batch size by 2 while doubling gradient accumulation steps (e.g., micro-batch 4 &amp; accum 4 &rarr; micro-batch 2 &amp; accum 8). Effective batch size (B_eff = b_micro * N_accum) is mathematically preserved.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="p-4 rounded-xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800">
      <div class="flex items-center justify-between mb-1">
        <span class="text-purple-400 font-bold font-mono">Level 3: Full Gradient Checkpointing Enforcement</span>
        <span class="text-xs font-mono text-gray-500">Memory Reduction: ~60%</span>
      </div>
      <p class="text-gray-300 text-xs leading-relaxed">
        Dynamically enables PyTorch activation recomputation across all attention heads and MLP projection layers. Rather than storing intermediate forward activations, they are recomputed during backward pass, reducing activation VRAM by 60% with a modest 15-20% compute overhead.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="p-4 rounded-xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800">
      <div class="flex items-center justify-between mb-1">
        <span class="text-purple-400 font-bold font-mono">Level 4: Sequence Length Batch Clamping</span>
        <span class="text-xs font-mono text-gray-500">Targeted Batch Recovery</span>
      </div>
      <p class="text-gray-300 text-xs leading-relaxed">
        If an isolated mini-batch triggers an OOM due to extreme sequence length, the healer isolates the spike batch, clamps token lengths to the 95th percentile, backpropagates safely, and logs the truncation event to the lineage ledger.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="p-4 rounded-xl bg-dark-950 border border-dark-800">
      <div class="flex items-center justify-between mb-1">
        <span class="text-purple-400 font-bold font-mono">Level 5: Checkpoint Rollback on Loss Divergence</span>
        <span class="text-xs font-mono text-gray-500">Loss Spike Protection</span>
      </div>
      <p class="text-gray-300 text-xs leading-relaxed">
        A moving exponential loss tracker monitors gradient stability. If step loss exceeds 3x moving average loss (EMA) or evaluates to NaN, training automatically rolls back to the last certified checkpoint, lowers the learning rate by 20%, and resumes.
      </p>
    </div>
  </div>

  <h2>CLI Invocation</h2>
  <p>
    Launch training with auto-heal enabled:
  </p>

  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-purple-300">
# Launch unattended training with the 5-step healer active
moro train --config ./moro.yaml --auto-heal
  </pre>

  <h2>Live Recovery Log Stream</h2>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-purple-300 leading-relaxed">
Step 420/1200 | Loss: 1.12 | VRAM: 7.9GB
[WARN] CUDA OOM at step 421 (token length 3,840)
[HEAL] Level 1: Flushed CUDA memory pool (Freed 820MB)
[HEAL] Level 2: Micro-batch 2 -> 1, Accum 8 -> 16
[RESUME] Checkpoint 400 reloaded
Step 421/1200 | Loss: 1.11 | VRAM: 6.1GB (STABLE)
Step 422/1200 | Loss: 1.09 | VRAM: 6.2GB
[SUCCESS] Full training finished with 0 data loss
  </pre>

  <div class="not-prose mt-12 pt-6 border-t border-dark-800 flex items-center justify-between">
    <a href="/docs/concepts/recipe-engine/" class="text-xs font-semibold text-gray-400 hover:text-white transition-colors">
      ← VRAM Recipe Predictor
    </a>
    <a href="/docs/concepts/eval-harness/" class="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-5 py-2.5 rounded-xl bg-moro-500 hover:bg-moro-400 text-white font-semibold text-xs transition-colors">
      <span>Multi-Layer Eval Harness</span>
      <ArrowRight class="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
    </a>
  </div>

## Document: /docs/cookbook/code-assistant/

<div class="not-prose mb-8">
    <span class="text-xs font-mono font-bold text-moro-400 uppercase tracking-wider bg-moro-500/10 px-2.5 py-1 rounded border border-moro-500/20 mb-3 inline-block">
      Cookbook Blueprint
    </span>
    <h1 class="text-3xl sm:text-5xl font-black text-white tracking-tight">Code Assistant</h1>
    <p class="text-gray-400 text-base mt-2">
      Train a specialized coding companion on your proprietary internal libraries, API client packages, and framework conventions.
    </p>
  </div>

  <h2>Training Data Best Practices</h2>
  <ol>
    <li><strong>Include PEP 484 Type Hints:</strong> Models trained on typed signatures hallucinate significantly fewer type mismatches.</li>
    <li><strong>Provide Complete Error Handling:</strong> Include <code>try / except</code> blocks and defensive edge-case checks in target completions.</li>
    <li><strong>Incorporate Sphinx/Google Docstrings:</strong> Ensures the model outputs comprehensive documentation for all generated functions.</li>
  </ol>

  <h2>Sample Training Data Format (JSONL)</h2>
  
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-sky-300 leading-relaxed">
cat &gt; data/raw/code_pairs.jsonl &lt;&lt; 'EOF'
{`{"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Write a Python function to reverse a string with type annotations"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "def reverse_string(s: str) -> str:\\n    \\"\\"\\"Reverse an input string safely.\\"\\"\\"\\n    return s[::-1]\\n\\n# Example usage:\\nassert reverse_string('hello') == 'olleh'"}]}`}
{`{"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain this code: for i in range(10): print(i)"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "This loop iterates over integers from 0 to 9 (exclusive of 10) and prints each integer to stdout using standard Python range semantics."}]}`}
EOF
  </pre>

  <h2>Evaluation Suite (eval_code.yaml)</h2>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-orange-300 leading-relaxed">
{`name: "code-assistant-eval"
tests:
  - id: "test_factorial"
    prompt: "Write a recursive Python function to compute the factorial of n."
    expected_keywords:
      - "def factorial"
      - "if n <= 1:"
      - "return"
    forbidden_terms:
      - "goto"
      - "as an AI model"`}
  </pre>

  <h2>Execution & Deployment</h2>
  <pre class="bg-dark-950 p-4 rounded-xl border border-dark-800 font-mono text-xs text-emerald-300 leading-relaxed">
# 1. Compile dataset
moro data build --source ./data/raw/code_pairs.jsonl

# 2. Train on local GPU
moro train --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct

# 3. Export to GGUF and deploy to Ollama
moro release export --run-id best --version v1.0.0
moro release deploy --target ollama --version v1.0.0 --name code-companion
  </pre>

  <div class="not-prose mt-12 pt-6 border-t border-dark-800 flex items-center justify-between">
    <a href="/docs/cookbook/json-extractor/" class="text-xs font-semibold text-gray-400 hover:text-white transition-colors">
      ← JSON Extractor
